notes:
### 1. Product Overview
Pylon is an AI-native B2B customer support and operations platform designed to unify customer conversations across multiple channels (such as Slack Connect, Microsoft Teams, email, chat widgets, Discord, and SMS) into a single ticketing inbox. It features autonomous AI agents and assistants to automate ticket pre-work and resolution, alongside "Account Intelligence" to aggregate CRM records and product usage data around customer accounts.

*   **Source URL:** `https://www.usepylon.com/schedule-demo`
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `...the agentic support platform ai & agents assist agent background agent slack agent support agent skills platform analytics & reporting account intelligence knowledge base workforce management surveys (nps & csat) ticketing channel & integrations slack microsoft teams discord telegram whatsapp phone & sms chat widget email`

---

### 2. Public API Authentication Methods
The public REST API exclusively uses static Bearer tokens generated from the admin dashboard. There is no public OAuth 2.0 application flow available for the REST API path. 

*   **Primary Auth Method for Multi-Tenant Integration:** `bearer_token`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication`
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `The pylon api uses bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your api token in the header of your request: copy authorization: bearer <token> generate an api token in the pylon dashboard .`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via Scalekit index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `The REST API accepts one thing: an admin-created Bearer token scoped to the whole organization. There is no OAuth on the API path and no per-user token.`

---

### 3. Credential Acquisition & Cost
*   **Access Category:** `partner_or_sales`
*   **How to get credentials:** Credentials can only be generated by an Admin user within an active Pylon workspace. There is no public self-serve developer signup or free developer sandbox; getting an account requires booking a demo or contacting sales.
*   **Cost:** API access is gated behind the paid Professional plan or higher. The Professional plan costs approximately $89/seat/month billed annually (or $118/seat/month billed monthly) and carries a mandatory 3-seat minimum, making the baseline cost at least $267/month. There is no permanent free tier.
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via Redpanda index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `In the Pylon dashboard, open the API tokens page at https://app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens... Only Pylon Admins can create tokens.`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via Unified.to index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `Pylon API access requires an Admin to generate an API token from a Pylon workspace; there is no self-serve developer sandbox.`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via QuantumDesk index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `Pylon pricing has three tiers: Starter ($59/seat), Professional ($89/seat), and Enterprise ($139/seat with 7-seat minimum). ... Public API access and webhooks are included in the Professional plan`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via Featurebase index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `Starter and Professional plans require 3 seats minimum... Professional at $89... API access and custom dashboards for exporting data and building tailored reports.`

---

### 4. API Style & Technical Details
*   **API Style:** REST API (via Redpanda index: `Wraps the Pylon REST API so an agent can:`)
*   **Breadth:** Broad. It covers a wide array of customer support and operations objects.
*   **OpenAPI Spec:** The official documentation uses GitBook with an interactive reference rather than hosting a standalone OpenAPI JSON/YAML file, though third-party OpenAPI specs exist (e.g., on apis.io: `openapi: 3.2.0 info: title: Pylon Contacts API...`).
*   **Webhooks:** Yes. Webhooks are supported and can be configured via Pylon's Trigger system.
*   **Sandbox:** No public self-serve developer sandbox is available.
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference`
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `documentation on available endpoints. accounts activities attachments audit logs call recordings contacts custom fields custom objects email feature requests issues knowledge base macros me messages surveys tags tasks & projects teams ticket forms training data user roles users`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via UsePylon Webhooks documentation)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `Webhooks fire on specific events inside Pylon and post to an endpoint you control... Go to Triggers in Settings and create a Trigger with the "Send webhook" action.`

---

### 5. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers
*   **MCP Category:** `official`
*   **Details:** Pylon publishes and hosts an official, managed MCP server at `https://mcp.usepylon.com` (launched in March 2026). It utilizes OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit) for per-user identity delegation over streamable HTTP. Community/third-party MCP servers also exist (e.g., StackOne).
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via UsePylon MCP documentation)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol... Server URL: https://mcp.usepylon.com. Auth: OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit).`
*   **Source URL:** `https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference` (via StackOne index)
*   **Verbatim Quote:** `StackOne's Pylon MCP server ships with 52 pre-built actions`

---

### 6. Buildability Verdict
*   **Verdict:** `ready_with_friction`
*   **Main Blocker:** `per_customer_admin_setup`
*   **Explanation:** The public REST API is fully documented and ready to be wrapped into an agent toolkit today. However, because there is no public OAuth 2.0 flow for the REST API path, the toolkit must rely on a manual per-customer admin setup where each user generates an organization-wide Bearer token from their dashboard and inputs it into Composio. Additionally, testing requires a paid plan (Professional tier or higher) since there is no free developer tier or sandbox.
